cues.en: Some of you may have heard this paradoxical fact about medical tests. It's very commonly used to introduce the topic of Bayes' rule in probability.
cues.zh: 你们中有些人可能听过医学检测的这个悖论性事实。它常被用来引出概率论中的贝叶斯法则。

cues.en: The paradox is that you could take a test which is highly accurate in the sense that it gives correct results to a large majority of the people taking it.
cues.zh: 这个悖论是：你可以做一项高度准确的检测，准确到对大多数受检者都能给出正确结果。

cues.en: And yet, under the right circumstances,
cues.zh: 然而，在合适的情况下，

cues.en: when assessing the probability that your particular test result is correct, you can still land on a very low number, arbitrarily low, in fact.
cues.zh: 在评估你这次检测结果正确的概率时，你仍可能得到一个非常低的数字，事实上可以任意低。

cues.en: In short, an accurate test is not necessarily
cues.zh: 简而言之，准确的检测不一定

cues.en: a very predictive test.
cues.zh: 就是很有预测力的检测。

cues.en: Now when people think about math and formulas, they don't often think of it as a design process. I mean, maybe in the case of notation, it's easy to see that different choices are possible. But when it comes to the structure of the formulas themselves and how we use them, that's something that people typically view as
cues.zh: 现在，人们想到数学和公式时，通常不会把它看作一个设计过程。我是说，也许在记号方面，很容易看出不同选择是可能的。但涉及公式本身的结构以及我们如何使用它们时，人们通常认为这是

cues.en: fixed.
cues.zh: 固定的。

cues.en: In this video, you and I will dig into this paradox, but instead of using it to talk about the usual version of Bayes' rule, I'd like to motivate an alternate version,
cues.zh: 在本视频中，你我将深入探讨这个悖论，但不会用它来讲通常版本的贝叶斯法则，而是想引出另一种版本，

cues.en: an alternate design choice.
cues.zh: 一种替代的设计选择。

cues.en: Now what's up on the screen now is a little bit abstract,
cues.zh: 现在屏幕上显示的内容有点抽象，

cues.en: which makes it difficult to justify that there really is a substantive difference here, especially when I haven't explained either one yet.
cues.zh: 这就很难证明这里确实存在实质区别，尤其是我还没解释其中任何一个。

cues.en: To see what I'm talking about, though, we should really start by spending some time a little more concretely and just laying out what exactly this paradox is.
cues.zh: 不过，要看清我在说什么，我们真该先花点时间更具体地铺开这个悖论到底是什么。

cues.en: Picture a thousand women and suppose that one percent of them have breast cancer.
cues.zh: 想象有一千名女性，假设其中百分之一患有乳腺癌。

cues.en: And let's say they all undergo a certain breast cancer screening and that nine of those with cancer correctly get positive results and there's one false negative.
cues.zh: 假设她们都接受某种乳腺癌筛查，其中九名患癌者正确得到阳性结果，还有一名假阴性。

cues.en: And then suppose that among the remainder without cancer, eighty nine get false positives and nine hundred and one correctly get negative results.
cues.zh: 再假设在其余未患癌的人中，八十九名得到假阳性，九百零一名正确得到阴性结果。

cues.en: So if all you know about a woman is that she does the screening and she gets a positive result, you don't have information about symptoms or anything like that, you know that she's either one of these nine true positives or one of these eighty nine false positives.
cues.zh: 所以，如果你对一个女性所知道的全部信息就是她做了筛查且结果为阳性，你并不了解症状或其他任何情况，你只知道她要么是这九名真阳性之一，要么是这八十九名假阳性之一。

cues.en: So the probability that she's in the cancer group given the test result is nine divided by nine plus eighty nine, which is approximately one in eleven.
cues.zh: 那么在给定检测结果的情况下，她属于癌症组的概率就是九除以九加八十九，约为十一分之一。

cues.en: In medical parlance, you would call this the positive predictive value of the test or PPV,
cues.zh: 用医学的话说，这叫做检测的阳性预测值，简称PPV，

cues.en: the number of true positives divided by the total number of positive test results.
cues.zh: 即真阳性数除以阳性检测结果总数。

cues.en: You can see where the name comes from. To what extent does a positive test result actually predict that you have the disease?
cues.zh: 你能看出这个名字的由来。一个阳性检测结果究竟在多大程度上能预测你确实患病？

cues.en: Now, hopefully, as I've presented it this way where we're thinking concretely about a sample population,
cues.zh: 希望我这样呈现——具体地考虑一个样本人群——

cues.en: all of this makes perfect sense.
cues.zh: 能让这一切变得完全合理。

cues.en: But where it comes across as counterintuitive
cues.zh: 但它之所以显得反直觉，

cues.en: is if you just look at the accuracy of the test, present it to people as a statistic, and then ask them to make judgments about their test result.
cues.zh: 是因为如果你只看检测的准确率，把它作为一个统计数据呈现给人们，然后让他们对自己的检测结果做出判断。

cues.en: Test accuracy is not actually one number, but two.
cues.zh: 检测准确率其实不是一个数字，而是两个。

cues.en: First, you ask, how often does a test correct on those with the disease? This is known as the test sensitivity,
cues.zh: 首先，你问：在有病的人身上，检测有多经常给出正确结果？这被称为检测敏感度，

cues.en: as in how sensitive is it to detecting the presence of the disease.
cues.zh: 也就是它对检测出疾病存在的敏感程度。

cues.en: In our example, test sensitivity is nine and ten or ninety percent. And another way to say the same fact would be to say the false negative rate is ten percent.
cues.zh: 在我们的例子里，检测敏感度是10分之9，即90%。同样的事实也可以换种说法：假阴性率是10%。

cues.en: And then a separate, not necessarily related number is how often it's correct for those without the disease,
cues.zh: 然后还有一个独立的、不一定相关的数字：在没有病的人身上，检测有多经常给出正确结果，

cues.en: which is known as the test specificity.
cues.zh: 这被称为检测特异度。

cues.en: As in, are positive results caused specifically by the disease,
cues.zh: 也就是说，阳性结果究竟是特异地由该疾病引起的，

cues.en: or are there confounding triggers giving false positives?
cues.zh: 还是存在混杂因素导致了假阳性？

cues.en: In our example, the specificity is about ninety one percent.
cues.zh: 在我们的例子里，特异度大约是91%。

cues.en: Or another way to say the same fact would be to say the false positive rate is nine percent.
cues.zh: 同样的事实也可以换种说法：假阳性率是9%。

cues.en: So the paradox here is that in one sense, the test is over ninety percent accurate. It gives correct results to over ninety percent of the patients who take it.
cues.zh: 所以这里的悖论是：从某种意义上说，检测准确率超过90%。它对超过90%的受检患者给出正确结果。

cues.en: And yet, if you learn that someone gets a positive result without any added information,
cues.zh: 然而，如果你得知某人得到了阳性结果，且没有额外信息，

cues.en: there's actually only a one in eleven chance that that particular result is accurate.
cues.zh: 那个特定结果准确的概率其实只有11分之1。

cues.en: This is a bit of a problem because of all of the places for math to be counterintuitive,
cues.zh: 这有点麻烦，因为在数学最容易反直觉的所有领域里，

cues.en: medical tests are one area where it matters a lot.
cues.zh: 医学检测恰恰是一个影响很大的领域。

cues.en: the psychologist Gerd Gigerrenzer gave a series of statistics seminars to practicing gynecologists,
cues.zh: 心理学家Gerd Gigerenzer给执业妇科医生做了一系列统计学讲座，

cues.en: and he opened with the following example.
cues.zh: 他以下面这个例子开场。

cues.en: A 50 year old woman, no symptoms,
cues.zh: 一位50岁女性，没有任何症状，

cues.en: participates in a routine mammography screening.
cues.zh: 参加了一次常规乳腺X光筛查。

cues.en: She tests positive,
cues.zh: 她的检测结果呈阳性，

cues.en: is alarmed, and wants to know from you whether she has breast cancer for certain or what her chances are. Apart from the screening result, you know nothing else about this woman.
cues.zh: 她惊慌失措，想从你这里知道她是否一定得了乳腺癌，或者她患病的概率有多大。除了筛查结果之外，你对这位女性一无所知。

cues.en: In that seminar, the doctors were then told that the prevalence of breast cancer for women of this age is about one percent,
cues.zh: 在那场研讨会上，医生们随后被告知，这个年龄段女性的乳腺癌患病率约为百分之一，

cues.en: and then to suppose that the test sensitivity is ninety percent and that its specificity was ninety one percent.
cues.zh: 然后假设检测灵敏度为百分之九十，特异度为百分之九十一。

cues.en: You might notice these are exactly the same numbers from the example that you and I just looked at. This is where I got them. So having already thought it through, you and I know the answer. It's about one in eleven.
cues.zh: 你可能注意到，这些数字和你我刚才看的例子完全相同。我就是从这里取的。所以经过一番思考，你和我都知道答案。大约是十一分之一。

cues.en: However, the doctors in this session were not primed with the suggestion to picture a concrete sample of a thousand individuals the way that you and I had. All they saw were these numbers.
cues.zh: 然而，这场研讨会上的医生们并没有像你和我那样，被引导去想象一个一千人的具体样本。他们看到的只是这些数字。

cues.en: They were then asked, how many women who test positive actually have breast cancer? What is the best answer? And they were presented with these four choices.
cues.zh: 然后他们被问到：检测呈阳性的女性中，实际有多少人患有乳腺癌？最佳答案是什么？他们面前有这四个选项。

cues.en: In one of the sessions, over half the doctors present said that the correct answer was nine 10,
cues.zh: 在其中一场研讨会中，超过一半的在场医生说正确答案是百分之九十，

cues.en: which is way off.
cues.zh: 这差得远了。

cues.en: Only a fifth of them gave the correct answer, which is worse than what it would have been if everybody had randomly guessed.
cues.zh: 只有五分之一的人给出了正确答案，这比所有人随机猜测的结果还要差。

cues.en: It might seem a little extreme to be calling this a paradox.
cues.zh: 把这件事称为悖论，可能显得有点极端。

cues.en: I mean, it's just a fact. It's not something intrinsically self contradictory.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，这只是一个事实。它本身并不是自相矛盾的东西。

cues.en: But as these seminars with Giga Renzer show, people, including doctors,
cues.zh: 但正如这些与 Giga Renzer 的研讨会所显示的，包括医生在内的人们，

cues.en: definitely find it counterintuitive that a test with high accuracy can give you such a low predictive value.
cues.zh: 确实会觉得反直觉：一个准确率很高的检测，竟然只能给出这么低的预测值。

cues.en: We might call this a veridical paradox,
cues.zh: 我们可以把这种情况称为真实性悖论，

cues.en: which refers to facts that are provably true, but which nevertheless can feel false when phrased a certain way. It's sort of the softest form of a paradox, saying more about human psychology than about logic.
cues.zh: 它指的是那些可以被证明为真、但换一种说法就会让人觉得不真实的事实。这算是悖论里最温和的一种形式，更多说明的是人的心理，而不是逻辑。

cues.en: The question is how we can combat this.
cues.zh: 问题在于，我们该如何应对这一点。

cues.en: Where we're going with this, by the way, is that I want you to be able to look at numbers like this and quickly estimate in your head that it means the predictive value of a positive test should be around one and eleven.
cues.zh: 顺便说一下，我们讲这些的目的，是想让你在看到这样的数字时，能快速在脑中估算出：阳性检测的预测值应该大约是一比十一。

cues.en: Or if I change things and ask, what if it was ten percent of the population who had breast cancer?
cues.zh: 或者如果我改一下条件，问：假如有百分之十的人群患乳腺癌呢？

cues.en: You should be able to quickly turn around and say that the final answer would be a little over fifty percent.
cues.zh: 你应该能很快反应过来，说最终答案会略高于百分之五十。

cues.en: Or if I said imagine a really low prevalence, something like zero point one percent of patients having cancer,
cues.zh: 或者如果我说，想象一个非常低的患病率，比如百分之零点一的患者患癌，

cues.en: you should again quickly estimate that the predictive value of the test is around one in a hundred, that one in a hundred of those with positive test results in that case would have cancer.
cues.zh: 你同样应该能快速估算出，检测的预测值大约是一百分之一，也就是说，在这种情况下，检测结果为阳性的人中大约只有百分之一真正患癌。

cues.en: Or let's say we go back to the one percent prevalence, but I make the test more accurate. I tell you to imagine the specificity is ninety nine percent.
cues.zh: 或者说回到百分之一的患病率，但我把检测做得更准确些。假设特异性是百分之九十九。

cues.en: There, you should be able to relatively quickly estimate that the answer is a little less than fifty percent.
cues.zh: 这样你应该能比较快地估算出答案略低于百分之五十。

cues.en: The hope is that you're doing all of this with minimal calculations in your head.
cues.zh: 希望你在做这些时，脑子里尽量少算。

cues.en: Now the goals of quick calculations might feel very different from the goals of addressing whatever misconception underlies this paradox, but they actually go hand in hand. Let me show you what I mean. On the side of addressing misconceptions,
cues.zh: 快速计算的目标，可能看起来和纠正这个悖论背后误解的目标很不一样，但它们其实是相辅相成的。让我解释一下。在纠正误解这方面，

cues.en: what would you tell to the people in that seminar who answered nine and ten? What fundamental misconception are they revealing?
cues.zh: 你会怎么跟研讨会上那些回答九和十的人说？他们暴露了什么根本性的误解？

cues.en: What I might tell them is that in much the same way that you shouldn't think of tests as telling you
cues.zh: 我可能会告诉他们，就像你不该把检测当成在告诉你

cues.en: whether you have a disease,
cues.zh: 你有没有病，

cues.en: you shouldn't even think of them as telling you your chances of having a disease.
cues.zh: 你甚至不该把它当成在告诉你患病的概率。

cues.en: Instead,
cues.zh: 相反，

cues.en: the healthy view of what tests do is that they update your chances.
cues.zh: 对检测作用的健康看法是，它在更新你的概率。

cues.en: In our example, before taking the test, a patient's chances of having cancer were one in a hundred. In Bayesian terms, we call this the prior probability.
cues.zh: 在我们的例子里，做检测之前，病人患癌的概率是百分之一。用贝叶斯的话说，这叫先验概率。

cues.en: The effect of this test was to update that prior by almost an order of magnitude up to around one in eleven.
cues.zh: 这个检测的作用是把先验概率更新了将近一个数量级，升到大约十一分之一。

cues.en: The accuracy of a test is telling us about the strength of this updating. It's not telling us a final answer.
cues.zh: 检测的准确度告诉我们的是这种更新的强度，而不是最终答案。

cues.en: What does this have to do with quick approximations?
cues.zh: 这和快速近似有什么关系？

cues.en: Well, a key number for those approximations
cues.zh: 嗯，这些近似的一个关键数字

cues.en: is something called the Bayes factor,
cues.zh: 叫做贝叶斯因子，

cues.en: and the very act of defining this number serves to reinforce this central lesson about reframing what it is the tests do.
cues.zh: 而定义这个数字的行为本身，恰恰强化了那个核心教训：重新审视检测到底在做什么。

cues.en: You see, one of the things that makes test statistics so very confusing is that there are at least four numbers that you'll hear associated with them. For those with the disease, there's the sensitivity and the false negative rate, and then for those without, there's the specificity and the false positive rate. And none of these numbers actually tell you the thing you want to know.
cues.zh: 你看，检测统计量之所以让人如此困惑，一个原因是你会听到至少四个与之相关的数字。对于患病的人，有灵敏度和假阴性率；对于未患病的人，有特异度和假阳性率。而这些数字没有一个真正告诉你你想知道的东西。

cues.en: Luckily,
cues.zh: 幸运的是，

cues.en: if you want to interpret a positive test result, you can pull out just one number to focus on from all this. Take the sensitivity divided by the false positive rate. In other words, how much more likely are you to see the positive test result with cancer versus without?
cues.zh: 如果你想解读一个阳性检测结果，你可以从这一堆里只挑出一个数字来关注。用灵敏度除以假阳性率。换句话说，有癌症时看到阳性结果的概率，是没癌症时的多少倍？

cues.en: In our example, this number is 10.
cues.zh: 在我们的例子里，这个数字是 10。

cues.en: This is the Bayes factor, also sometimes called the likelihood ratio.
cues.zh: 这就是贝叶斯因子，有时也叫似然比。

cues.en: A very handy rule of thumb is that to update a small prior or at least to approximate the answer, you simply multiply it by the Bayes factor. So in our example, where the prior was one in a 100, you would estimate that the final answer should be around one in 10, which is in fact slightly above the true correct answer.
cues.zh: 一个非常方便的经验法则是：要更新一个很小的先验，或者至少近似出答案，你只需把它乘以贝叶斯因子。所以在我们的例子里，先验是百分之一，你可以估计最终答案大约是十分之一，而实际上这略高于真正正确的答案。

cues.en: So based on this rule of thumb, if I asked you what would happen if the prior from our example was instead one in a thousand,
cues.zh: 所以根据这个经验法则，如果我问你，把我们例子里的先验概率换成千分之一会怎样，

cues.en: You could quickly estimate that the effect of the test should be to update those chances to around one in a hundred.
cues.zh: 你可以很快估算出，检测的效果应该会把患癌概率更新到大约百分之一。

cues.en: And in fact, take a moment to check yourself by thinking through a sample population.
cues.zh: 事实上，你可以花点时间，通过思考一个样本群体来验证一下。

cues.en: In this case, you might picture ten thousand patients where only ten of them really have cancer.
cues.zh: 在这个情况下，你可以想象一万名患者，其中只有十个人真正得了癌症。

cues.en: And then based on that ninety percent sensitivity,
cues.zh: 然后基于那百分之九十的敏感度，

cues.en: we would expect nine of those cancer cases to give true positives.
cues.zh: 我们会预期这些癌症病例中有九个给出真阳性。

cues.en: And on the other side, a ninety one percent specificity
cues.zh: 另一方面，百分之九十一的特异度

cues.en: means that nine percent of those without cancer are getting false positives.
cues.zh: 意味着那些没有癌症的人中有百分之九会得到假阳性。

cues.en: So we'd expect nine percent of the remaining patients, which is around nine hundred, to give false positive results.
cues.zh: 所以我们预期剩余患者中的百分之九，大约九百人，会给出假阳性结果。

cues.en: Here, with such a low prevalence,
cues.zh: 在这里，患病率如此之低，

cues.en: the false positives really do dominate the true positives. So the probability that a randomly chosen positive case from this population actually has cancer is only around one percent,
cues.zh: 假阳性确实压倒了真阳性。所以从这个群体中随机选出的一个阳性病例真正患癌的概率只有大约百分之一，

cues.en: just like the rule of thumb predicted.
cues.zh: 正如经验法则所预测的那样。

cues.en: Now this rule of thumb clearly cannot work for higher priors. For example, it would predict that a prior of 10%
cues.zh: 现在这个经验法则显然不适用于更高的先验概率。例如，它会预测先验为10%

cues.en: gets updated all the way to 100% certainty, but that can't be right. In fact, take a moment to think through what the answer should be, again, using a sample population.
cues.zh: 会被一直更新到百分之百的确定性，但这不可能对。事实上，花点时间想想答案应该是什么，同样用样本群体来思考。

cues.en: Maybe this time we picture ten out of a hundred having cancer.
cues.zh: 也许这次，我们假设一百人中有十人患癌。

cues.en: Again, based on the ninety percent sensitivity of the test, we'd expect nine of those true cancer cases to get positive results.
cues.zh: 同样，基于检测百分之九十的灵敏度，我们预期这些真正患癌的病例中有九个会得到阳性结果。

cues.en: But what about the false positives? How many do we expect there?
cues.zh: 但假阳性呢？我们预计会有多少？

cues.en: About nine percent of the remaining ninety, about eight.
cues.zh: 大约百分之九的剩余九十人，大约八个。

cues.en: So upon seeing a positive test result, it tells you that you're either one of these nine true positives or one of the eight false positives.
cues.zh: 所以当看到阳性检测结果时，它告诉你，你要么是这九个真阳性之一，要么是八个假阳性之一。

cues.en: So this means the chances are a little over fifty percent,
cues.zh: 这意味着几率略高于百分之五十，

cues.en: roughly nine out of seventeen or fifty three percent.
cues.zh: 大约是十七分之九，即百分之五十三。

cues.en: At this point, having dared to dream that Bayesian updating could look as simple as multiplication,
cues.zh: 此时，你大胆梦想贝叶斯更新能像乘法一样简单，

cues.en: you might tear down your hopes and pragmatically acknowledge sometimes life is just more complicated than that.
cues.zh: 你可能会放下希望，务实承认有时生活就是更复杂。

cues.en: Except it's not. This rule of thumb turns into a precise mathematical fact as long as we shift away from talking about probabilities
cues.zh: 但其实不然。这个经验法则转化为精确的数学事实，只要我们不再谈论概率

cues.en: to instead talking about odds.
cues.zh: 转而谈论几率。

cues.en: If you've ever heard someone talk about the chances of an event being one to one or two to one, things like that, you already know about odds.
cues.zh: 如果你听过有人谈论事件几率是一比一或二比一之类的，你已经了解几率了。

cues.en: With probability, we're taking the ratio of the number of positive cases out of all possible cases. Right? Things like one in five or one in ten. With odds, what you do is take the ratio of all positive cases to all negative cases.
cues.zh: 用概率，我们取阳性病例数占所有可能病例数的比率。对吧？比如五分之一或十分之一。用几率，你取所有阳性病例与所有阴性病例的比率。

cues.en: You commonly see odds written with a colon to emphasize the distinction,
cues.zh: 你经常会看到用冒号书写的比值，以强调两者的区别，

cues.en: but it's still just a fraction, just a number.
cues.zh: 但它仍然只是一个分数，只是一个数字。

cues.en: So an event with a 50% probability would be described as having one to one odds.
cues.zh: 所以一个概率为 50% 的事件，会被描述为 1 比 1 的比值。

cues.en: A 10% probability is the same as one to nine odds.
cues.zh: 10% 的概率等同于 1 比 9 的比值。

cues.en: An 80% probability is the same as four to one odds. You get the point.
cues.zh: 80% 的概率等同于 4 比 1 的比值。你懂这个意思。

cues.en: It's the same information. It still describes the chances of a random event, but it's presented a little differently, like a different unit system.
cues.zh: 这是同样的信息。它仍然描述随机事件发生的可能性，只是呈现方式稍有不同，就像不同的单位制。

cues.en: Probabilities are constrained between zero and one with even chances sitting at 0.5,
cues.zh: 概率被限制在 0 和 1 之间，均等机会位于 0.5，

cues.en: but odds range from zero up to infinity with even chances sitting at the number one.
cues.zh: 但比值从 0 一直延伸到无穷大，均等机会位于数字 1。

cues.en: The beauty here is that a completely accurate, not even approximating things way to frame Bayes rule is to say, express your prior using odds, and then just multiply by the Bayes factor.
cues.zh: 这里的美妙之处在于，一种完全准确、甚至无需近似的方式来表述贝叶斯法则，就是：用比值来表达你的先验，然后直接乘以贝叶斯因子。

cues.en: Think about what the prior odds are really saying. It's the number of people with cancer divided by the number without it. Here, let's just write that down as a normal fraction for a moment so we can multiply it. When you filter down just to those with positive test results, the number of people with cancer gets scaled down, scaled down by the probability of seeing a positive test result given that someone has cancer.
cues.zh: 想想先验比值真正在说什么。它是患癌人数除以未患癌人数。这里，我们暂时把它写成一个普通分数，以便相乘。当你筛选到仅有阳性检测结果的人时，患癌人数会被缩小，缩小的因子是在某人患癌的前提下看到阳性检测结果的概率。

cues.en: And then similarly, the number of people without cancer also gets scaled down, this time by the probability of seeing a positive test result, but in that case.
cues.zh: 然后类似地，未患癌人数也会被缩小，这次缩小的因子是在那种情况下看到阳性检测结果的概率。

cues.en: So the ratio between these two counts, the new odds upon seeing the test, looks just like the prior odds except multiplied by this term here,
cues.zh: 这两个计数之间的比值，也就是看到检测结果后的新几率，看起来就像先验几率，只不过乘上了这一项，

cues.en: which is exactly the base factor.
cues.zh: 这一项正是基础因子。

cues.en: Look back at our example where the Bayes factor was 10. And as a reminder, this came from the ninety percent sensitivity divided by the nine percent false positive rate. How much more likely are you to see a positive result with cancer versus without?
cues.zh: 回看我们那个贝叶斯因子为 10 的例子。提醒一下，它来自 90% 的灵敏度除以 9% 的假阳性率。有癌症相比没有癌症，看到阳性结果的可能性高多少倍？

cues.en: If the prior is one percent, expressed as odds, this looks like one to ninety nine.
cues.zh: 如果先验是 1%，写成几率，就是 1 比 99。

cues.en: So by our rule, this gets updated to 10 to 99,
cues.zh: 按我们的规则，它会被更新为 10 比 99，

cues.en: which if you want, you could convert back to a probability. It would be 10 divided by 10 plus 99 or about one and eleven.
cues.zh: 如果愿意，你可以再换算回概率。就是 10 除以 10 加 99，约等于十一分之一。

cues.en: If instead, the prior was 10%,
cues.zh: 如果先验是 10%，

cues.en: which was the example that tripped up our rule of thumb earlier,
cues.zh: 也就是之前让我们那条经验法则出错的例子，

cues.en: expressed as odds, this looks like one to nine.
cues.zh: 写成几率，就是 1 比 9。

cues.en: By our simple rule, this gets updated to 10 to nine, which you can already read off pretty intuitively.
cues.zh: 按我们的简单规则，它会被更新为 10 比 9，这个结果你已经很直观地读出来了。

cues.en: It's a little above even chances, a little above one to one.
cues.zh: 它略高于五五开，略高于 1 比 1。

cues.en: If you prefer, you can convert it back to a probability. You would write it as ten out of nineteen
cues.zh: 如果你愿意，可以把它换算回概率。写成 19 分之 10，

cues.en: or about 53%.
cues.zh: 也就是约 53%。

cues.en: And indeed, that is what we already found by thinking things through with a sample population.
cues.zh: 确实，这正是我们用样本总体推演后已经得到的结果。

cues.en: Let's say we go back to the one percent prevalence, but I make the test more accurate. Now what if I told you to imagine that the false positive rate was only one percent instead of nine percent?
cues.zh: 假设回到 1% 的患病率，但我把检测变得更准确。现在如果我让你设想，假阳性率只有 1%，而不是 9%，会怎样？

cues.en: What that would mean is that our Bayes factor is ninety instead of 10. The test is doing more work for us. In this case, with the more accurate test, it gets updated to 90 to 99,
cues.zh: 这意味着我们的贝叶斯因子是90而不是10。这个检测为我们做了更多的工作。在这种情况下，有了更准确的检测，它更新为90比99，

cues.en: which is a little less than even chances, something a little under 50%.
cues.zh: 这略低于均等机会，略低于50%。

cues.en: To be more precise, you could make the conversion back to probability and work out that it's around forty eight percent. But, honestly, if you're just going for a gut feel, it's fine to stick with the odds.
cues.zh: 更精确地说，你可以转换回概率并计算出大约是百分之四十八。但说实话，如果你只是想要一个直观感觉，坚持用几率就可以了。

cues.en: Do you see what I mean about how just defining this number helps to combat potential misconceptions?
cues.zh: 你明白我的意思吗？仅仅定义这个数字就有助于消除潜在的误解。

cues.en: For anybody who's a little hasty in connecting test accuracy directly to your probability of having a disease, it's worth emphasizing that you could administer the same test with the same accuracy
cues.zh: 对于那些急于将检测准确率直接等同于患病概率的人，值得强调的是，你可以对多个不同的患者进行相同的检测，准确率相同，

cues.en: to multiple different patients who all get the same exact result. But if they're coming from different contexts,
cues.zh: 他们都会得到完全相同的结果。但如果他们来自不同的背景，

cues.en: that result can mean wildly different things.
cues.zh: 那个结果可能意味着截然不同的事情。

cues.en: However, the one thing that does stay constant in every case is the factor by which each patient's prior odds get updated.
cues.zh: 然而，在每种情况下都保持不变的一件事是每位患者的先验几率被更新的因子。

cues.en: And by the way, this whole time we've been using the prevalence of the disease, which is the proportion of people in a population who have it, as a substitute for the prior, the probability of having it before you see a test. However, that's not necessarily the case. If there are other known factors, things like symptoms or in the case of a contagious disease, things like known contacts,
cues.zh: 顺便说一下，我们一直使用疾病的流行率，即人群中患病者的比例，作为先验的替代，即在你看到检测结果之前患病的概率。然而，情况不一定如此。如果有其他已知因素，比如症状，或者在传染病的情况下，比如已知接触者，

cues.en: those also factor into the prior, and they could potentially make a huge difference.
cues.zh: 这些也会纳入先验，并且可能产生巨大的差异。

cues.en: As another side note, so far, we've only talked about positive test results, but way more often, you would be seeing a negative test result.
cues.zh: 顺便提一句，到目前为止我们只讨论了阳性结果，但更多时候你碰到的其实是阴性结果。

cues.en: The logic there is completely the same, but the base factor that you compute is gonna look different. Instead, you look at the probability of seeing this negative test result with the disease versus without the disease.
cues.zh: 其中的逻辑完全一样，但计算出的贝叶斯因子会有所不同。此时你要看的是，患病与未患病情况下出现阴性结果的概率比。

cues.en: So in our cancer example, this would have been the ten percent false negative rate divided by the ninety one percent specificity
cues.zh: 所以放在刚才癌症的例子里，就是用 10% 的假阴性率除以 91% 的特异度，

cues.en: or about one in nine. In other words, seeing a negative test result in that example would reduce your prior odds by about an order of magnitude.
cues.zh: 大约是九分之一。换句话说，在那个例子中，阴性检测结果会让你的先验几率降低约一个数量级。

cues.en: When you write it all out as a formula, here's how it looks. It says your odds of having a disease given a test result equals your odds before taking the test, the prior odds, times the Bayes factor.
cues.zh: 如果把它写成公式，就是这个样子：已知检测结果时患病的几率，等于检测前的几率（即先验几率）乘以贝叶斯因子。

cues.en: Now let's contrast this with the usual way that Bayes rule is written, which is a bit more complicated.
cues.zh: 现在我们把它与贝叶斯定理的常规写法对比一下，后者要更复杂一些。

cues.en: In case you haven't seen it before, it's essentially just what we were doing with sample populations, but you wrap it all up symbolically.
cues.zh: 如果你以前没见过，它本质上就是我们刚才对样本群体所做的计算，只不过全用符号包装了起来。

cues.en: Remember how every time we were counting the number of true positives and then dividing it by the sum of the true positives and the false positives?
cues.zh: 还记得我们每次是怎么数出真阳性人数，再除以真阳性与假阳性之和的吗？

cues.en: We do just that, except instead of talking about absolute amounts, we talk of each term as a proportion.
cues.zh: 公式做的完全就是这件事，只不过把绝对数量换成了比例形式。

cues.en: So the proportion of true positives in the population comes from the prior probability of having the disease multiplied by the probability of seeing a positive test result in that case.
cues.zh: 所以人群中真阳性的比例，等于患病的先验概率乘以在这种情况下看到阳性检测结果的概率。

cues.en: And then we copy that term down again into the denominator, and then the proportion of false positives comes from the prior probability of not having the disease times the probability of a positive test in that case.
cues.zh: 然后把这一项再抄到分母里，接着假阳性的比例，等于没有患病的先验概率乘以在这种情况下检测为阳性的概率。

cues.en: If you want, you could also write this down with words instead of symbols if terms like sensitivity and false positive rate are more comfortable.
cues.zh: 如果你更习惯“敏感性”和“假阳性率”这些说法，也可以用文字而不是符号把它写下来。

cues.en: And this is one of those formulas where once you say it out loud, seems like a bit much, but it really is no different from what we were doing with sample populations.
cues.zh: 这是那种一念出来好像有点复杂的公式，但它其实和我们用样本群体做的东西没什么不同。

cues.en: You wanted to make the whole thing look simpler, you often see this entire denominator written just as the probability of seeing a positive test result overall.
cues.zh: 为了让整个式子看起来更简单，你常会看到整个分母就写成总体上看到阳性检测结果的概率。

cues.en: While that does make for a really elegant little expression,
cues.zh: 虽然这确实能构成一个非常优雅的小表达式，

cues.en: if you intend to use this for calculations,
cues.zh: 但如果你打算拿它来做计算，

cues.en: it's a little disingenuous.
cues.zh: 就有点不实在了。

cues.en: Cause in practice, every single time you do this, you need to break down that denominator into two separate parts, breaking down the cases.
cues.zh: 因为在实践中，每次你这么做，都得把那个分母拆成两个独立部分，按情况分解。

cues.en: So taking this more honest representation of it, let's compare our two versions of Bayes' rule. And, again, maybe it looks nicer if we use the words sensitivity and false positive rate. If nothing else, it helps emphasize which parts of the formula are coming from statistics about the test accuracy.
cues.zh: 那么，采用这个更诚实的表示，我们来比较一下贝叶斯法则的两个版本。再说一次，如果用“敏感性”和“假阳性率”这些词，可能会更好看。至少，它有助于强调公式中哪些部分来自关于检测准确率的统计数据。

cues.en: I mean, this actually emphasizes one thing I really like about the framing with odds and a Bayes' factor, which is that it cleanly factors out the parts that have to do with the prior and the parts that have to do with the test accuracy.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，这其实凸显了我很喜欢用几率和贝叶斯因子来构建问题的一个原因：它能干净地把与先验有关的部分和与测试准确率有关的部分分开。

cues.en: But over in the usual formula, all of those are very intermingled together, and this has a very practical benefit. It's really nice if you wanna swap out different priors and easily see their effects. This is what we were doing earlier. But with the other formula, to do that, you have to recompute everything each time. You can't leverage a precomputed Bayes factor the same way.
cues.zh: 但在通常的公式里，这些全都混在一起，而这样做有很实际的好处。如果你想换不同的先验并轻松看到它们的影响，这真的很好用。这就是我们之前在做的事。但用另一个公式，要这么做，你每次都得重新计算所有东西。你没法同样地利用预先算好的贝叶斯因子。

cues.en: The odds framing also makes things really nice if you wanna do multiple different Bayesian updates based on multiple pieces of evidence. For example, let's say you took not one test but two, or you wanted to think about how the presence of symptoms plays into it.
cues.zh: 如果你想基于多条证据做多次不同的贝叶斯更新，几率框架也让事情变得很顺手。比如，假设你不是做了一次测试而是两次，或者你想考虑症状的存在与否如何影响结果。

cues.en: For each piece of new evidence you see, you always ask the question, how much more likely would you be to see that with the disease versus without the disease?
cues.zh: 对于你看到的每一条新证据，你总是问这个问题：在有病的情况下看到它的可能性，比没病时高多少？

cues.en: Each answer to that question gives you a new Bayes factor, a new thing that you multiply by your odds.
cues.zh: 这个问题的每个答案都会给你一个新的贝叶斯因子，一个新的、用来乘到你几率上的东西。

cues.en: Beyond just making calculations easier, there's something I really like about attaching a number to test accuracy that doesn't even look like a probability.
cues.zh: 除了让计算更容易，我还真的很喜欢给测试准确率附上一个甚至看起来不像概率的数字。

cues.en: I mean, if you hear that a test has, for example, a nine percent false positive rate, that's just such a disastrously ambiguous phrase. It's so easy to misinterpret it to mean there's a 9% chance that your positive test result is false.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，如果你听说一个测试有，比如说，9%的假阳性率，这个说法实在太模糊了，简直是灾难。很容易被误解为你的阳性结果有9%的概率是假的。

cues.en: But imagine if instead the number that we heard tacked on to test results was that the Bayes factor for a positive test result is, say, 10.
cues.zh: 但设想一下，如果检测结果附带的数字，是阳性检测的贝叶斯因子——比方说是 10。

cues.en: There's no room to confuse that for your probability of having a disease. The entire framing of what a Bayes factor is is that it's something that acts on a prior. It forces your hand to acknowledge the prior as something that's separate entirely and highly necessary to drawing any conclusion.
cues.zh: 这样就绝不会把它误当成你患病的概率了。贝叶斯因子的整个构架，就是作为一个作用在先验概率上的东西。它迫使你承认，先验概率是完全独立存在的，而且对得出任何结论都至关重要。

cues.en: All that said, the usual formula is definitely not without its merits. If you view it not simply as something to plug numbers into,
cues.zh: 话虽如此，常规公式也绝非毫无可取之处。如果你不单把它当作套入数字的公式，

cues.en: but as an encapsulation
cues.zh: 而是看作一种概括提炼，

cues.en: of the sample population idea that we've been using throughout,
cues.zh: 融入了我们从头到尾一直在用的样本总体思想，

cues.en: you could very easily argue that that's actually much better for your intuition.
cues.zh: 你完全可以说它其实更有助于建立直觉。

cues.en: After all, it's what we were routinely falling back on in order to check ourselves that the Bayes factor computation even made sense in the first place.
cues.zh: 毕竟，我们之前就是反复退回到这一步，来核验贝叶斯因子的计算从一开始是否说得通。

cues.en: Like any design decision, there is no clear cut objective best here, but it's almost certainly the case that giving serious consideration to that question will lead you to a better understanding of Bayes' rule.
cues.zh: 就像任何设计决策一样，这里并没有绝对客观的最优解，但可以肯定的是，认真思考这个问题能帮你更好地理解贝叶斯法则。

cues.en: Also, since we're on the topic of kind of paradoxical things, a friend of mine, Matt Cook, recently wrote a book all about paradoxes.
cues.zh: 另外，既然聊到了这类略带悖论色彩的话题，我的朋友 Matt Cook 最近写了一本专门讲悖论的书。

cues.en: I actually contributed a small chapter to it with thoughts on the question of whether math is invented or discovered, And the book as a whole is this really nice connection of thought provoking paradoxical things ranging from philosophy to math and physics. You can, of course, find all the details in the description.
cues.zh: 我其实也为这本书贡献了一个小章节，探讨数学究竟是被发明还是被发现的，而整本书则精彩地串联起了从哲学到数学、物理等各个领域发人深省的悖论。详情当然可以在简介里找到。
